written: 2026-11-09, before any mediation number was computed (dry runs on a random tiny model only)
question: Does the harmful signal created by Tashon's MLP weight edits (MLP-only 256 arrows, model 1 = em seed_0) travel through attention at floors 14 and 16 (0-indexed)?
pairs: Tashon's split.json TEST ids (382). His race used 323 = test ids that also passed his AI-reviewer check (valid_pairs.json), which is not in git or any repo we can read, so we use the 382 superset. Per-pair numbers are saved with ids so the 323 subset can be recomputed if valid_pairs.json appears.
answer_positions: positions whose next-token prediction is scored by the ruler (the n positions before the last), as in the ruler

definitions.closed(X): (R_B - R_X) / (R_B - R_N), ratio of means over pairs
definitions.moved(X, site): 1 - sum_pairs d_X / sum_pairs d_B, where d_X = sum over the pair's 2 sequences of the Frobenius norm over answer positions of (activation_X - activation_N) at that site
definitions.swap_effect(X, P): (R_X - R_{X with attention outputs at floors P replaced by N's}) / (R_B - R_N); same denominator in B and B-M so they are comparable
definitions.blocked(P): (R_{N+M} - R_{N+M with attention outputs at floors P replaced by N's}) / (R_{N+M} - R_N)
definitions.CI: 95% percentile bootstrap over pairs, 2000 resamples, seed 0; differences use paired resamples

controls.also_reported_not_in_rule: MLP outputs of floors 14 and 16 (moved), neighbour attention floors 13 and 15, all 36 floors

gates (stop if any fails).G1_zero_removed_is_B: arrow-built B vs PEFT-merged B on the first 32 test pairs: |mean R diff| < 0.01, every per-pair |R diff| < 0.03, answer-position argmax agreement >= 0.99
gates (stop if any fails).G2_all_removed_is_N: all arrows removed: weights identical to base Aya and max |logit diff| == 0 on 3 sequences
gates (stop if any fails).G3_reproduce_tashon: on the 382 test pairs: |closed(B-M) - 0.421| <= 0.05 and |made(N+M) - 0.726| <= 0.05 (his numbers are on 323 of these 382 pairs, measured with batched forward hooks; tolerance chosen for that). Also reported: closed(B-S) vs his 0.538, and our per-pair R_B / R_N vs his ruler files (target mean diff < 0.02).

rule_hypothesis_A_supported.i_moved: moved(B-M, attn14) >= 0.5 AND moved(B-M, attn16) >= 0.5 AND min(moved14, moved16) - max(moved at attn 5, 25, 30) >= 0.15 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI of that difference above 0
rule_hypothesis_A_supported.ii_mediation: swap_effect(B-M, {14,16}) <= 0.5 * swap_effect(B, {14,16}) (point estimate; ratio CI reported)
rule_hypothesis_A_supported.iii_blocking: blocked({14,16}) >= 0.5 AND blocked({14,16}) - max(blocked({5,25}), blocked({25,30})) >= 0.15 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI of that difference above 0
rule_hypothesis_A_supported.verdict: all three pass = supported; one or two pass = partly supported (say which); none = not supported

own_weights_vs_input (descriptive, no pa: closed(B-A1416) and moved(B-A1416, attn14/16) compared with moved(B-M, attn14/16)

amendments.type: post-hoc change to an implementation gate (G1 only); approved by Shreya after the first run stopped at G1
amendments.what_changed: G1's top-1 (argmax) agreement criterion (>= 0.99) is now measured with both models in fp32 instead of bf16. G1's two bf16 harm-score criteria (|mean R diff| < 0.01, every per-pair |R diff| < 0.03), G2, G3 and the hypothesis rule (i)-(iii) are unchanged. bf16 argmax agreement is still computed and reported, for the record only.
amendments.reason: Likely (not proven) cause: in bf16 the arrow-built B rounds once after an fp32 add, while PEFT forms the delta in bf16, so near-tied top tokens flip; the harm-score criteria agreed (mean R diff -0.0006). The 0.99 bf16 threshold was set without checking it against the earlier precedent below.

evidence.precedent: circuitkit_audit diff_patch.py: bf16 argmax agreement 0.969 between two correct implementations (HF vs TL port), fp32 agreement > 0.995
